size.note: Shoulder height (38–48 cm), head-and-body length (67.3–81.2 cm, rounded here to 67–81 cm) and mass (6–13 kg) follow Wikipedia (citing Kingdon 2013 for mass). Animal Diversity Web gives a lower mass range of 5–10 kg, an average shoulder height of about 38 cm (not entered as a range), and only a loose total length of nearly a metre. The Wikipedia ranges are entered; the ADW disagreement is noted. No published tail-length range was found. Skinner and Chimimba (2005, p. 487, Table 260.1, two samples combined) give a tail of 25–39.5 cm.

summary: A medium-sized jackal with reddish flanks and legs, a sharply defined black-and-silver saddle, and a black-tipped tail. It is widespread and often seen by day in Kruger, including along roads and near kills.
description: The black-backed jackal has a slender body, a pointed muzzle and fairly large pointed ears. The back is a distinct saddle of black mixed with silver hair, set against reddish to tawny flanks and legs. The tail is bushy and black at the tip. Sexes are similar in colour.
habits: It is typically monogamous and territorial. Pairs or family groups hunt and forage, and helpers may stay on to raise later litters. It is opportunistic and often active by day as well as at night. In southern Africa it is highly vocal, advertising with a high-pitched howl and giving sharp yelps in alarm.

diet.summary: An opportunistic carnivore and scavenger. It takes small mammals, birds, reptiles, insects, fruit and carrion, and will also take young antelope when it can.

young: In southern Africa, mating is usually between May and August. Gestation is about 60 days. Litters average about four pups, of which often only one to three survive. Older offspring may help at the den. Skinner and Chimimba (2005, p. 490) give a gestation of about 60 days and, for Kruger, births from August to October (citing Fairall 1968).
habitat: Open woodland, savanna and grassland, including road verges and the edges of rest camps. It uses a wide range of habitats as long as there is cover and food.

similar.note: The side-striped jackal is greyer, has a pale stripe along the side, and has a white tail tip rather than a black one. It lacks the sharply defined silver-and-black saddle.
The bat-eared fox is smaller, with much larger ears, a greyish coat and no black saddle.

population.notes: No Kruger population figure was found. The EWT 2025 assessment says there are no accurate regional estimates, and that more than 10,000 animals occur in the assessment region as a whole; that figure is not Kruger-specific.

viewNotes.note: The black-and-silver saddle is sharply set off from the reddish flanks, and the tail tip is black.

calls.description: In southern Africa the species is highly vocal. Sounds include yelping, woofing, whining, growling and cackling. A high-pitched whining howl is used to advertise, and the alarm is an explosive cry followed by short, high-pitched yelps.
